kevin: Heads-up — after the 5.19 kernel bump on the private VPC cluster I noticed a ~12-18ms p95 increase on short-gen workloads (seq len ~64). Can someone sanity-check whether this is env-related or a runtime regression?

sanjay: Can you paste the exact config you ran and the model + batch size? quick check: was cpu governor changed or irq affinity reset?

kevin: model=gpt-small-open, batch=1, temperature=0. No governor change in our infra patches AFAIK. Test command I ran:
```
curl -sS -X POST https://private-runner.internal/v1/generate \ 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \ 
  -d '{"model":"gpt-small-open","input":"hello","max_new_tokens":64}'
```
Logs: saw token latency jump after kernel upgrade window at ~2026-11-02T02:00Z.

infra-bot: automated-bench — private-cluster-7: completed 2026-11-02T03:05Z. Summary: short-gen p95 increased from 22.4ms -> 35.6ms; long-gen stable. Artifacts: https://artifacts.internal/runs/2026-11-02/bench-2082123456

olivia: tagging runtime and infra: @sanjay @lisa. If it's IRQ/cpuaffinity we can try isolcpus+nohz_full on a node and rerun. Also want to rule out NUMA/memory alloc changes after the kernel bump.

lisa: I can run perf and a flamegraph on one affected node. Which binary to sample — the runtime process (redwood-runtime) or the container shim (rundir)? Prefer sampling the runtime JIT paths.

sanjay: sample both. Useful commands:
```
sudo perf record -F 99 -a -g --pid=$(pgrep redwood-runtime) -- sleep 60
sudo perf script | ./FlameGraph/stackcollapse-perf.pl > out.folded
./FlameGraph/flamegraph.pl out.folded > perf.svg
```
Also collect /proc/interrupts and `irqbalance status`.

kevin: run-id attached in artifact. I also captured /proc/interrupts before+after upgrade. One suspicious thing: softirqs on eth0 jumped.

lisa: ok spinning up a single-node repro with kernel 5.19 and 5.15 to compare. ETA ~40m. I’ll post perf.svg and a short diff of top stacks.

infra-bot: note: we have an active canary pool with 5.19; autoscaler will move low-priority Dedicated VMs into canary this afternoon. Recommend pausing autoscale until repro done.

olivia: paused autoscale for private-cluster-7 per infra-bot. @kevin pls confirm any customer-facing workloads affected.

kevin: none customer-facing; internal e2e tests only. :thumbsup:

lisa: first flamegraph uploaded: https://artifacts.internal/perf/perf-2082123456.svg — top hotspot is in skb checksum path and XPS transmit. Suspect NIC offload differences with 5.19 driver.

sanjay: if offload changed, we might see more softirq wakeups. Try toggling GRO/TSO on the host: `ethtool -K eth0 gro off tso off gso off` and rerun the bench. If latency improves, it's driver/offload.

kevin: running that now on node-7. Rerun command returning p95 ~24ms (back to baseline). Will leave offload disabled on canary until patch.

olivia: great signal. Next steps: file a kernel-driver ticket with NIC vendor, add a runtime mitigation (prefer kernel-level offload toggles in node bootstrap), and add a short-term CI test that runs short-gen latency after kernel updates.

kevin: opening internal ticket INF-4921 with perf artifacts + /proc/interrupts diff. Assigning to networking and eng-runtime.

lisa: also documenting the one-liner to toggle offloads in our infra runbook.

sanjay: thanks all. If anyone wants me to automate the toggle as a temporary scheduler job, I can prototype.

kevin: yes please, prototype job would be ideal. Closing loop later today.

infra-bot: reminder: benchmark artifacts TTL = 30d.
